div.p: Multi-processor System-on-Chip (MPSoC) based on Networks-On-Chip (NoC) as a communication paradigm becoming an industry standard in design of embedded system. Some class of embedded systems are designed for executing realtime services which are having stringent deadlines, failing to meet these deadlines may lead to catastrophic failure. NoC not only requires specialized architecture to deal with real time requirement but also problem of task mapping and flow priority assignment becomes more crucial. Real-time schedulability analysis is performed assuming worst-case to get the lower bound of schedulability for tasks and flows. The term schedulability defines the number of tasks and flows meeting the deadlines. Flow of data packets from source to destination node depends on the network topology of NoC and routing strategy at the routers. It improves on end to end schedulability by considering all possible minimal paths on place of fixed X-Y routing. It also considers deadlock avoidance in routing.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Multi-processor System-on-Chip design have multiple IP cores, processing elements executing multiple task simultaneously. These elements communicate with each other. Network-on-chip (NoC) provides a router based inter-connect platform for communication among the cores with features of scalability, flexibility and reusability [1], [2]. Fundamental design aspects of NoC based multi-core system are mapping the tasks of an application to the cores, giving priorities to tasks and flows, routing strategy and arbitration policy. These aspects are required to be optimized with maximization of utilization of system resources and minimization of the energy consumption. Also, in real-time systems, additional measures like task response times and end-to-end latencies of flows are to be considered. The performance of targeted design not only depends on the correctness of the communication but also on meeting the deadline. In order to support real-time traffic, the predictability of end to end delay needs to be guaranteed [3]. NoC design starts with an application specification in the form of a task graph which gives detail of all the tasks in the application and the communication flow between them. System-on-Chip performance depends on the topology and mapping of the tasks of an application on available processing elements (PEs) as per network topology. Mapping decisions are based on dependencies of communication among the tasks and inter-connect platform of multi-core system. , as a fixed method, some of the flows may miss the deadlines. To explore the impact of non-deterministic routing, minimal routing algorithm is developed and to counter the impact of deadlock, avoidance has been considered. The algorithm is effective for routing when more than one minimal path exists between sender and receiver [4]. Prediction of latencies is important to support the deadline bounds. Latencies are partially non-deterministic due to network contention in real-time NoC. This contention can be improved by alternate routing methodology as shown in Fig 3.

The problem statement of the paper is to maximize the schedulability so that all tasks and communication flows in the real-time application meet their deadline by optimizing task mapping, flow priority and flow routes. Section III discusses mathematical model for analysis of schedulability in case of real-time NoC. Section IV discusses about minimal routing and deadlock avoidance. Section V contains a combined genetic algorithm for mapping, priority assignment and routing. Section VI gives comparison results with X-Y routing. Section VII presents scope of future work and conclusive remarks.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: Literature review of task mapping, priority assignment and routing in case of NoC based MPSoC is summarized in this section. Keeping Real-Time performance as prime concern, the work related to worst-case schedulability analysis has been reviewed and followed. Mapping techniques have been extensively researched, some of the mapping techniques are provided in [5], [6] and [7]. Song et al. [8] proposed implementation of virtual channels to deal preemptions among traffic flows. Shi and Burns [9] further worked on the scheme with assumptions of per-traffic-flow distinctive priorities and per-priority virtual channels. The work of Shi et al. in [9] proposes worst-case analysis for priority preemptive NoCs having wormhole switching. Shi et al. [10] extended the work for priority assignment of real-time wormhole communication in on-chip networks. The model given by Shi et al. in [11] became go-to method for analysis of schedulability in case of real-time NoC. Shi and Burn covered the task mapping with schedulability analysis in [12]. A novel approach has been proposed in [13] as a technique to determine an energy efficient priority assignment and routing algorithm. Real-time communication model for on-chip network in [11] is further analyzed in [14]. Xiong et al. in [15] has presented that the model may become pessimistic and results in incorrect network delay upper-bound. Revision of analysis in [16] improves the previous model by classification of upstream and downstream interferences. The above mentioned works assume deterministic X-Y routing policy. The possibility of having nondeterministic routing is not considered much. However as mentioned in section I, deterministic X-Y routing can increase contention [17]. [18] and [19] describes the advantages of having non-deterministic routing for fault tolerance and side channel attack resilience respectively.

div.head: III. SYSTEM MODEL
div.p: Schedulability of the application is attributed to guarantee of deadline satisfaction of the tasks to the certain extent. Prediction of latencies in a two dimensional NoC due to contention is important to schedulability analysis. A

processing core can execute one task at a time from multiple tasks might be allocated to it. Deterministic XY routing and random routing with possible minimal path has been considered for implementation to see their respective effect on schedulability. Typical application model representation is done by task set and communication of messages between tasks. Application Model can be characterized by computation load and communication traffic of an application. It is assumed that a task transmits a message only after its execution is completed and the overhead of the network interface is negligible. A traffic flow represents a series of packets sent over the NoC from source task to destination task. Each task and flow is represented with following attributes: Task = {c, t, p, d} and Flow = {P, C, T, D, J R } Here, c is task execution time, t is inter-arrival interval, p is task priority and d is deadline. Similarly for each message flow, P is flow priority, C is basic latency, T is flow release interval, D is deadline and J R is release jitter. It is assumed that flow deadline is same as source task deadline which is less than or equal to task period.

For worst case schedulability analysis, end-to-end latencies are calculated considering maximum contention in the network. For this, worst case analysis proposed in [9], [11] has been used. In the paper it is assumed that the worst case network latency occurs when all the tasks arrive simultaneously, means all packets from the traffic-flow are fired at same time. The basic network latency C i , of flow is the time a flow takes to reach its destination under zero network contention and is given by equation C i = (L imax + L add )/f size * f size /B link + H.S Where L imax is the volume of communication, L add is the additional header and tail flit information, f size is the flit size, B link the link bandwidth, H is the number of hops that the flow must take and S is the processing delay of each router. div.head: IV. MINIMAL ROUTING AND DEADLOCK AVOIDANCE
div.p: An important work by Nikolic et al. [17] focuses on minimal path and possible non deterministic routing in case of wormhole switch NoC. It can be presumed that, deterministic X-Y routing is probable to increase contention more. In this work, the focus is on deriving minimal flow-paths i which do not governed by any fixed routing policy.

The minimal path i defined between the source router In the modified BFS, instead of storing only one predecessor, we keep track of all predecessors that give minimum distance. For finding paths, we then backtrack using all these predecessors. try to turn left and end up in a cyclic wait. Deadlocks can be detected, and their happening can be broken or avoided, but it is better to avoid situation of deadlocks by choosing routing techniques that prevent cyclic acquisition. In Fig. 6, avoidance of one of the packets turn would result in deadlock prevention. This indicates that a routing algorithm can possibly avoid deadlock in a direct network by not allowing certain turns. The turn model [20] is one of the popular methods of deadlock avoidance. The turn model prohibits the minimum number of turns that break all of the cycles to avoid the deadlock. The turn model concept is used in few partially adaptive routing algorithms for twodimensional meshes, for example west-first, north-last, and negative-first. Use of any of these routing algorithms results in uneven adaptiveness, at least half of the source-destination pairs can have single minimal path, while full adaptiveness is provided for other half of the pairs [21]. Uneven adaptiveness is not fair and also limits the ability of the model to alleviate traffic congestion. In this work, odd-even turn model is used for better adaptiveness. The odd-even turn model restricts certain turns on specific locations so that a circular wait does not occur. It is based on two rules. Rule-1: EN turn for any packet is not allowed at a node located in an even column, and NW turn for any packet is not allowed at a node located in an odd column. Rule-2: ES turn for any packet is not allowed at a node located in an even column, and SW turn for any packet is not allowed at a node located in an odd column. The model is deadlock free with prevention of 180 ο turns, which is applicable here as work in the paper considers minimal routes only.

div.head: V. GENETIC ALGORITHM FOR COMBINED MAPPING, PRIORITY ASSIGNMENT AND ROUTING
div.p: Genetic Algorithm (GA) is a widely used method to solve problem of optimization in various domain. It is an evolutionary meta-heuristic population of candidate solutions is evolved over generations to find the fittest solution. Genetic operators like cross-over and mutation are used to drive evolution process. The chromosome structure defines element to be optimized and fitness function defines its formulation.

We have considered two fitness functions. The first and the main fitness function is the best possible schedulability of application, optimising the mapping, flow priority assignment and flow routing between cores. The second one is the minimisation of network congestion. A typical chromosome structure is shown in Fig. 7. Chromosome can be divided into three parts viz. task mapping, flow priority and flow routes. The size of a single chromosome is therefore, number of tasks + 2*number of flows. In the flow route part, we consider a real number between 0 and 1. This number is then multiplied with the total number of routes possible. The integer part of the real number obtain is the route number that the flow will take. ii. For parent selection, the population is ranked as per fitness value and pairs are randomly chosen from percentage of top population. iii. GA operators, Cross-over and Mutation are applied for convergence and exploration of solution space. These operators are applied separately for mapping, flow priority and flow route part of chromosomes. iv. Single point ordered cross-over is applied for Priority assignment. Single point cross-over is applied on Mapping and No cross-over applied for flow route. v. For Mutation, Two random indices are swapped, and this can be done multiple times as mutation required. vi. To avoid the chances of losing the best solutions during the evolution process, top 3 individuals are carried over to the next generation. Crossover pool is taken Top 30% population, individuals mutation rate is 0.7, decreased as GA evolves, Population Size taken as 500 and 500 Generations. vii. To make the optimization faster convergence with better schedulability, information from the task graphs like communication volume, task and flow deadlines, and interdependency of tasks are considered relevant and experimentally derived heuristics are used. viii. Cross-over is applied for priority assignment and mapping parts of a chromosome randomly depending on a crossover probability. Cross-over is not applied for flow route. Similarly Mutation is also applied on first two parts randomly while Mutation is always applied for flow route. ix. After every few generations, mappings of the top particles were chosen, and heuristics for these elite mappings were calculated and inserted into the population as new candidates, with the same mapping as the top individuals. x. There is a secondary objective as minimization of network congestion as defined as follows: Network Congestion = w 1 * Link Contention + w 2 *Router Contention+w 3 *Non-uniform load penalty If no. of tasks mapped on core is Ni, the penalty of core i = 0, if N i =1 = N i 3, otherwise The value for constant w 1 , w 2 , w 3 are found by iterative experimentation as w 1 =0.2, w 2 =0.1, w 3 =0.9.

div.head: VI. RESULTS
div.p: To evaluate the suitability of GA, an application with 25 tasks and 42 communication flow has been considered. Genetic algorithm as given in section V is used to optimise task mapping and flow priorities for different NoC sizes. The schedulability achieved by optimising only mapping and priority and keeping routing fixed to X-Y was found. Then for the same application and different NoC size, Genetic algorithm was used to optimise task mapping, flow priority and minimal routes. Random routes with minimal distances were chosen so that schedulability increases. From Fig. 8 it can be seen that having non-deterministic minimal routing considerably improved the schedulability. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK In this paper a Genetic Algorithm based approach has been reported that perform mapping of tasks, assigns priorities to tasks and flows while also finding non deterministic minimal routes. It has been established that schedulability of tasks improves significantly for real-time applications. As multiple minimal routes for each flow exist, we have probabilistic value for flow taking particular routes and thus, the interference set will also have probabilities. Considering these probabilities, equations for calculating schedulability can be modified to provide average-case analysis. Future work also involves extending the work for dynamic real-time system.
